h1: Awa Koh Chang — A Modern Design Resort with a Long Pool Running to the Sea on Kai Bae Beach
intro: If your mental image of a Koh Chang resort is old wooden bungalows by the sand, Awa Koh Chang tears that up · A 4-star boutique resort built around crisp modern lines — white, grey and timber — with a long pool that runs straight from the lobby down toward the sea, in the heart of Kai Bae Beach · Opened in 2014 as a sister property to The Dewa · Around 120 modern rooms with soft beds and generous space · The draws here are the design, the pool, and a central location you can walk from · From approx. ฿1,800/night, scoring 8.9 from around 460 reviews

body.html: Awa Koh Chang sits at the northern end of Kai Bae Beach, the popular stretch in the middle of Koh Chang · The first thing guests mention is the design — clean modern lines, sharp edges, a white-grey-timber palette, nothing like the wooden bungalows you find all over the island · The highlight is a long pool that runs straight from the building down toward the sea, which is the single most-photographed feature in reviews.

The roughly 120 rooms come in several tiers — Superior Hillside (40 sqm) sits in a garden annex across the road, Deluxe and Deluxe Premium (54 sqm) sit inside the resort on the pool/sea side, and it goes up to the Beachfront Suite (108 sqm) · Most rooms are spacious and modern with a balcony · What guests consistently praise is how comfortable the beds are and how clean the rooms feel · Worth knowing: the Hillside rooms are across the road, so it's a short crossing to the pool and sea — if you want to be poolside, book Deluxe or above.
"Modern, clean room, super-comfortable bed, a beautiful long pool, and you walk straight out of the resort onto Kai Bae's mid-beach restaurants — great value for a 4-star."

The star here is the long outdoor pool running toward the sea, ringed with sun loungers and a bar · The vibe is social and lively rather than dead-quiet — good if you like being poolside with people around · There's a spa for massages and treatments, a beachfront restaurant and bar, and a buffet breakfast that reviewers rate as solid · One note from reviews: in high season the pool and common areas can get fairly busy.

The honest caveat is that the beach directly in front isn't the best part of Kai Bae · At the northern tip, low tide exposes rocks and muddy sand, so swimming is less comfortable than the middle and southern sections · Many guests use the pool as their base and stroll to a better stretch of beach to swim · If you're a dedicated beach-lounger who wants to swim right outside your room, this spot may not fit — but if you're here for the pool, the design and a great location, it barely matters.

Location is a real strength — you're in the heart of Kai Bae Beach, about a 5-minute walk to its cluster of restaurants, convenience stores and bars · It's roughly 10–15 minutes by car to White Sand Beach and about 10 minutes to Klong Prao · Getting here from Bangkok means driving to the Trat-side piers, taking the ferry across to Koh Chang, then a songthaew or taxi to Kai Bae · A score of 8.9 from around 460 Trip.com reviews is strong and steady for a 4-star on Koh Chang.

The straight verdict: Awa Koh Chang is one of the best-value picks among modern design resorts on Kai Bae Beach · Spacious rooms, soft beds, a handsome pool, a central walkable location and friendly pricing · The trade-offs to accept are the so-so beach at low tide right in front, the Hillside rooms being across the road, and a busy pool when the resort is full · If those three sit fine with you, the value here is hard to match in a 4-star on this island.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: if you want to be by the pool and sea, book Deluxe or above — don't just grab the cheapest Hillside rate without realising you'll be crossing the road · Time your sea swims with the tide; it's easier at high water · For high season (November–February), book ahead and lock a free-cancellation rate first, then compare across platforms · The rainy season is quieter and cheaper on Koh Chang, but some days bring strong surf — check the forecast before you go.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Awa Koh Chang

faq.q: Where is Awa Koh Chang and what's nearby?
faq.a: The resort sits at the northern end of Kai Bae Beach, in the middle of Koh Chang, Trat Province · It's about a 5-minute walk to Kai Bae's cluster of restaurants and bars · Around 10 minutes by car to Klong Prao Beach and 10–15 minutes to White Sand Beach · Getting here means a ferry across to Koh Chang, then a short drive to Kai Bae.

faq.q: How much does Awa Koh Chang cost and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rates start at approximately ฿1,800/night for a Superior Hillside (40 sqm, garden annex across the road) · It steps up through Deluxe and Deluxe Premium (54 sqm, inside the resort on the pool/sea side) to the Beachfront Suite (108 sqm) · High-season rates climb quickly, so compare across platforms before booking.

faq.q: Is the beach in front of Awa Koh Chang good for swimming?
faq.a: The beach out front is the northern tip of Kai Bae, and at low tide it has rocks and muddy sand, so swimming is less comfortable than the mid and southern sections · Many guests use the pool as their main base and walk to a better stretch to swim · If you do go in the sea, it's easier at high tide.

faq.q: Who is Awa Koh Chang best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who want a modern 4-star design resort with a fine pool and a central location at a fair price · Good for couples, groups of friends and families who prioritise the pool and convenience and like walking to restaurants · It's not a dead-quiet retreat or a spot for swimming straight off your doorstep.

faq.q: Which room should I choose, and how is the Hillside different?
faq.a: If you want to be by the pool and sea, choose Deluxe or above, as those sit inside the resort on the pool side · The cheapest Superior Hillside rooms are in a garden annex across the road, so you cross over to reach the pool/sea · If you don't mind the crossing and want to save, Hillside is still good value.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book, and how do I get there?
faq.a: For high season (November–February), book about 3–6 weeks ahead as it's a popular Kai Bae resort · From Bangkok, drive to the Trat-side piers, take the ferry across to Koh Chang, then a songthaew to Kai Bae · Pick a Free Cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm, and compare across platforms.
